advances: Structural compatibility and cap error for centrally symmetric fibers, with a deformation preserving mixed volume.
author: PK-research-agent
proof:
Compatibility is $\delta+D\subseteq L_p$. Reflecting gives $-\delta+D\subseteq L_p$, and the convex hull of those two translates is $D+[-\delta,\delta]$, which also contains the first translate. Support functions add for Minkowski sums, giving the equivalence with the support inequalities.

On a line parallel to $e$ over the projection of $D$, the interval of $D+[-\delta,\delta]$ has length greater than that of $D$ by $2\|\delta\|$, with unchanged projection. Cavalieri's formula gives the volume reserve. On the same lines, translating $D$ by $\delta$ changes the length captured by a halfline by at most $\|\delta\|$ and changes nothing when the halfspace trace is the whole line or empty. Integration proves the cap estimate. In coordinates centered at $c_p$, a through-$c_p$ cap bisects $D$ and tests $D+\delta$ for the interpolated body, so its error is bounded by half the reserve. For sharpness choose $D=[-1,1]\times[-1/2,1/2]^{d-1}$, $\delta=t e_1$ for $0<t\le1$, and $L_p=D+[-\delta,\delta]$. The cap $x_1\le0$ of $D+\delta$ has volume $1-t$ compared with $1$ at its own center, and the reserve is $2t$. This is a compatible interpolation, for example by taking two equal endpoint fibers $D+\delta$ and the middle fiber $L_p$ at bases $-1,0,1$.

Under deformation each representation has center defect $t\delta$, since the affine contribution cancels. The segment containment puts $D+t\delta$ in $L_p$, establishing every compatibility relation. Any point in the hull at an old integer base is a convex combination of placed fiber points, and grouping by base gives one of these compatible Minkowski combinations. Thus the exact section is the prescribed one. The projected hull is $\operatorname{conv}P$, which contains precisely $P$ among integer bases by completeness of the original projection. Translations preserve volumes and symmetry. If $P$ affinely spans, full-dimensional continuous fibers at spanning bases together affinely span the ambient space, so their hull has interior.
statement:
For a finite set of integer bases $P$ with compact full-dimensional centrally symmetric fibers $K_z=c_z+L_z$, $L_z=-L_z$, fix any representation $p=\sum_i\lambda_i z_i$ of a base $p\in P$, where $z_i\in P$, $\lambda_i\ge0$, and $\sum_i\lambda_i=1$. Put $D=\sum_i\lambda_iL_{z_i}$ and $\delta=\sum_i\lambda_i c_{z_i}-c_p$. Compatibility $\sum_i\lambda_i K_{z_i}\subseteq K_p$ is equivalent to
$$
D+[-\delta,\delta]\subseteq L_p
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
h_{L_p}(u)\ge\sum_i\lambda_i h_{L_{z_i}}(u)+|u\cdot\delta|\quad\text{for every }u.
$$
For $\delta\ne0$ and $e=\delta/\|\delta\|$, let $A_e=|\operatorname{proj}_{e^\perp} D|_{d-1}$, with $A_e=1$ in dimension one. Then $|K_p|-|D|\ge2\|\delta\| A_e$. For every closed halfspace $H$, the volumes of $D\cap H$ and $(D+\delta)\cap H$ differ by at most $\|\delta\| A_e$; this translation estimate holds for any nonempty compact convex $D$. In a compatible representation each through-$c_p$ cap of $\sum_i\lambda_i K_{z_i}$ differs from half its volume by at most $(|K_p|-|D|)/2$, with coefficient $1/2$ sharp. For $\delta=0$ the reserve is nonnegative and the cap difference is zero.

If $P$ is the complete integer projection of a convex body with such fibers, then for any affine $a$ the fibers $a(z)+t(c_z-a(z))+L_z$, $-1\le t\le1$, have the same volumes and occur as the exact integer fibers of their lifted convex hull, with projection having no new integer bases. The hull has interior when $P$ affinely spans the base space.
title: Exact compatibility, cap error and deformation for symmetric fibers
